Get up-to-date step outputs from outside pipelines

Source: R/pipeline.R
pub_out.Rd

Returns the output of a step like x[[step, "out"]], but only if the step is "done", i.e. up to date in its own pipeline. Otherwise, it signals an error or returns an error item (see on_error).

In a single pipeline, a layout step arranges the outputs of other steps into a document with pub_doc(), and pipeflow handles inputs that failed or are outdated. When a document combines the outputs of several pipelines that are run separately, nothing does. pub_out() closes that gap, so that error objects, old results or missing outputs never end up in a document.

Usage

pub_out(x, step, on_error = c("stop", "item"))

Arguments

x

A pipeflow pipeline or view.

step

character(1) name of the step.

on_error

What to return if the step is not done because of a failure: "stop" signals an error, "item" returns an error item.

Value

The output of step, or an error item (class pub_error). For a step that failed for some partition keys and on_error = "item", its partitioned output with an error item for each failed key.

Details

Steps that are not done

  • A step that failed (state "failed"): its output is the error condition.

  • A step skipped because a step it depends on failed (state "outdated" or "new"): it keeps its earlier output or has none.

  • A step that did not run yet after a change, e.g. of its parameters or of a step it depends on (state "outdated"), or that was just added (state "new"): it keeps its earlier output or has none.

What pub_out() does then

  • on_error = "stop": an error of class pubflow_not_done names the pipeline, the step, its state and the failed steps it depends on.

  • on_error = "item": for the first two cases, an error item is returned. A document shows it as an error box, like a failed input of a layout step (see pub_doc()), while pub_render() refuses it unless the report spec allows error items. The third case is always an error, as no failure is involved.

The message is the one of the failed step's last attempt. A step that failed itself is named as the cause, otherwise the first failed step it depends on (failures before a step that is done, e.g. one that recovered with ~try(), don't count).

Split steps

A step downstream of a step with exec = "split" runs once per partition key and can fail for some keys only. It then keeps the outputs of the keys that succeeded.

  • on_error = "item" returns the partitioned output with an error item for each failed key, so a document shows the results of the other keys and one error box per failed key.

  • on_error = "stop" signals an error that names the failed keys.

See also

pub_doc()

Examples

test_pipeline <- function(name, values) {
    pipeflow::pip_new(name) |>
        pipeflow::pip_add("data", \(values = 1) values) |>
        pipeflow::pip_add("mean", \(x = ~data) {
            if (anyNA(x)) stop("missing values")
            mean(x)
        }) |>
        pipeflow::pip_add("content", \(m = ~mean) {
            pub_text(paste("Mean:", pub_format_num(m, 2)))
        }) |>
        pipeflow::pip_set_params(list(values = values))
}
tests <- list(
    Assay = test_pipeline("Assay", c(99.1, 98.7)),
    Water = test_pipeline("Water", c(0.4, NA))
)
for (p in tests) {
    suppressWarnings(
        pipeflow::pip_run(p, lgr = NULL, on_error = "continue")
    )
}

pub_out(tests$Assay, "content")
#> [1] "Mean: 98.90"
try(pub_out(tests$Water, "content"))
#> Error in pub_out(tests$Water, "content") : 
#>   The output of step 'content' of pipeline 'Water' is not up to date (state "new").
#> ✖ Step 'mean' failed: missing values

# One section per test; the failed one shows an error box
parts <- lapply(tests, pub_out, step = "content", on_error = "item")
pub_doc(parts, title = "Tests")
#> <pubflow document> "Tests"
#> # Assay
#>   text "Mean: 98.90"
#> # Water
#>   error "step 'mean' of pipeline 'Water' failed: missing values"
